body:
[A594] TAKEN
Branch: `640-m8a` from dev `e8454e2751d05b02ee8e5a571857589ab358ab86` (local, not pushed). Executor [A594]; reviewers [R606] (internal) and [R607] (external).
Authoritative references: assignment [6100371426](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-6100371426); `docs/design/MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md` "L11 The SoC side" and "Firmware and block RAM ledger"; owner decisions D4 ([5991591637](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5991591637)) and the 224 KB firmware block RAM ([6081706413](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-6081706413)); manager rulings D3 and D7 ([5990755268](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-5990755268)); the F5 size ruling ([#665 6081705916](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/665#issuecomment-6081705916)); M0s STOP ([6087021702](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-6087021702)); `docs/testing/PP_SHADOW_BASELINE_RECIPE.md`; `docs/design/AREA_BUDGET.md`.
Interpreted scope: under the existing split switch (`--ctrl-mailbox`) only, replace LiteDRAM main memory with on-chip block RAM for the control firmware, reusing the BIOS ROM and SRAM the ledger credits, inside 50 RAMB36 including stack, static pools, shape-sized staging and the descriptor image. The all-fabric default stays digest-identical. Edits stay in the memory map and memory instantiation. No CPU, register-map or default-behaviour change.
Validation plan: first the memory-fit proof, because the assignment makes a shape that does not fit a STOP: link the firmware at the shipping 1x1 and the largest shape (one and two interfaces) at this base, map the on-chip memory those spans need in Vivado (RAMB36/RAMB18 and usable bytes), and confirm the BIOS ROM/SRAM reuse count at this checkpoint. Then, only if every shape fits: the planted controls, the service checks (`check_nvm_capture.py` 8x8, host tests, `nvm_cosim`, `nvm_capture_cpu`, builder and deploy gates, a split-image simulation boot) and the M0s route under the lock.
Blockers: two prerequisites look absent at this base and will be confirmed in the evidence. The split switch adds an idle mailbox and keeps the wrapper (`hdl/milan/milan_datapath.sv:8003`), and no image boots the control application (F-INT PR 2 is not merged). M0s has no split figure ([6087021702](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/640#issuecomment-6087021702)).

[A10] **Ruling on [A594]'s STOP (6101473717).**

1. **The binding limit is the owner's 224 KB, not 50 tiles.** The owner's decision (6081706413) is 224 KB of firmware block RAM. "About 50 RAMB36" converted that at 4.5 KB per tile, which counts parity. The plan already says 224 KiB is 56 tiles at 4 KiB usable. Your largest shape (8x8 with two interfaces, 221,728 B) is inside 224 KB, so no shape is bounded and no firmware is cut.
   - The firmware allocation is up to 56 RAMB36 as mapped.
   - Because M8a is split-placement only, the ledger takes the conditional release of the wrapper's storage (-11 tiles), which the split build removes.
   - The ledger after release must stay at or under 121.5, with the 13.5 reserve untouched.
2. **No power-of-two waste.** Map the firmware memories at what they need: split ROM and RAM banks sized to the image, a `ram_decomp` or equivalent style, or a depth that is not a power of two built from smaller banks. The four points must reach their floor or close to it. Report RAMB36 and RAMB18 as mapped.
3. **The firmware owns the reset entry in the split placement.** The BIOS ROM and SRAM are not kept there (about 10 tiles). The all-fabric image keeps its BIOS unchanged. State the boot console and diagnostics that the split image loses or keeps.
4. **Sequencing: two steps.**
   - **M8a-1 now:** the memory map and instantiation behind `--ctrl-mailbox`, and the fit proof.
     - Out-of-context mapping at all four points with items 1-3.
     - The linked spans.
     - The ledger rows with measured values.
     - The planted controls: an over-budget allocation, a memory-map overlap and a wrong-shape staging buffer.
     - The all-fabric default is digest-identical.
     
     Post REVIEW READY for M8a-1 as a reviewable PR.
   - **M8a-2 after F-INT PR 2 merges:** the split-image simulation boot, the service checks (`check_nvm_capture.py` 8x8, `nvm_cosim`, `nvm_capture_cpu`), and the integrated route through the M0s recipe with its split figure.
   - If items 1-3 still do not fit at the largest shape, STOP with the table.

[A10] **M8a-1 round 5: re-measure the fit for the merged firmware.** R606-4 ([6118557490](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/721#issuecomment-6118557490)) and R607-4 ([6118122865](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/721#issuecomment-6118122865)) are NEGATIVE at `8ab2b539`. Both report the same MINOR finding. The dev merge brought F-INT and the lwSRP adoption, which grow all four linked firmware images. The documented fit still describes the earlier images; for example, the largest ROM now needs a fifth bank. Executor [A594].

- **Re-measure on the merged images.** Re-run the four linked-image points (`ctrl_srp_image.py --with-aecp --layout split`, both shapes and both interface counts) with a recorded runtime. Then run the isolated mapping (`syn/ooc/ctrl_memory_ooc.py` and its focused synthesis recipe) on those images.
- **Reconcile the documents with the new receipts:** the fit table, the memory-ledger rows and the headroom statements in `SPLIT_CONTROL_MEMORY.md`, `MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md` and `AREA_BUDGET.md`. Keep earlier figures only with their source named.
- **Limits.** Each image must stay within the 56-tile planner limit and the 224 KB firmware limit. STOP if either is exceeded.
- The runtime stack-protector workaround is #723's; use the reviewers' `-fno-stack-protector` probe only as they did, and record it.
- Re-run both reviewers' probes (`run_fit.py` and `compare_fit.py`).

This round needs no integrated route and no boot. Post REVIEW READY (or STOP) with the head.
